text: The title serves as a strong introduction, drawing attention to the topic, which focuses on the application of large language models in education.

This example adds practical relevance and credibility to the research. The statistic strengthens the argument by demonstrating student interest and demand for AI skills.

While the ethical concerns are mentioned, they are vague and lack specific examples or a connection to the research focus. Providing concrete examples of privacy or algorithmic bias issues in education would strengthen this section.

This is somewhat vague and would benefit from more specific examples of "effective digital teaching strategies" or references to previous successful implementations.

The literature review is well-justified as a starting point. To make this part more robust, consider explaining how the findings from the review will inform the subsequent stages of the research, such as the experimental approach or interviews.

This is a promising strategy. It would be beneficial to provide examples of the kind of teachers or institutions targeted for interviews. Additionally, elaborating on how the insights from these interviews will directly shape the research outcomes could enhance the clarity of this section.

The choice of an experimental approach is appropriate for comparing methods. However, specifying more details about the experimental setup, such as the duration of the experiment, the nature of the tasks, and how variables like bias are controlled, would make this part more thorough.
